speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am the adviser for Singapore Swimming Association and the past President for Singapore Table Tennis Association.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If I were to ask the question, "Are we a sporting nation?", I am sure some will say yes, some will say no.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Yes, because many exercise stations in our residential precincts and many brisk-walk groups.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have Vision 2030, and we have Olympic gold medal and Paralympic gold medals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But many would still say, "No, we have yet to be a sporting nation".

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, the episode on "live" telecast of the Olympic Games.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We nearly missed the opportunity to witness "live" the historic moment presented by our Joseph Schooling.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Immediately, there was a lot of response on the ground.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A lot of discussions in the coffeeshops, friends' gatherings, and a lot of my residents asked me, "Is our Government too calculative?" And they said that we can afford to pay hundreds of millions for the English Premier League, and yet, we cannot afford to pay for a "live" telecast of the Olympics.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And I have residents who even suggested, "Why do we not collect $1 from each of us?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Six million people, $6 million!" And for those of you who are sporting fans, you will know it is miles apart – a lot of difference between watching a "live" telecast and a delayed telecast.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If you already know the results, the excitement is no longer there.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We, as a nation, send athletes to compete in the Olympics were not prepared to fork out money for a "live" telecast.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, we proclaim we know the importance and the value of sports in unifying people, in inspiring people, and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We must not leave this to a commercial decision.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For a first-world nation, it is almost unthinkable if Singaporeans are denied of this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some joked that they have to go to neighbouring countries during the Olympics period.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We are well-known for 	Page: 109 planning ahead and I am sure we can do it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second reason is National Service (NS) deferment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I had lunch with May and Colin Schooling before May left for Rio.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have known May for a long time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: From time to time, she would share with me the challenges and problems that she is facing.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: During that lunch, she shared with me her No 1 headache at that time, that is, Joseph Schooling's NS deferment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It gave people the impression that our Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) is high-handed, too rigid, and they will tell you the answer when they are ready to give you the answer.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And MCCY gave people the impression that either they have no power or are not interested.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And some civil servants even think that Olympic medals are not important.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, our poor Joseph Schooling was under great pressure, not just to prepare for the Olympics, but he had to deal with the problem of whether he needed to come back for NS, after end-August.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Luckily, he turned pressure into strength, and the rest is history.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Following his win, there has been an outpouring of support for greater flexibility of NS deferment for local athletes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, parents are still left unsure if they should support their sons in their desire to pursue their sporting dream or whether they should take the proven route and get back to the academic road.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In Korea, all male citizens are required to undergo 21 months of compulsory military service.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was told that Korean athletes representing their country get to decide when they serve their national service, so long as they serve before they turn 30 years old.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As in the case of Singapore, the issue is a thorny one.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The conscription law in Korea states that those who have contributed significantly to the nation through athletic or artistic skills are exempted from military duties.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The only requirement is that they must go through four weeks of combat training.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This law currently exempts athletes who win a medal at the Olympics or finish first in the Asian Games.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In Singapore, the number of athletes falling under this group is very small.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For the Rio Olympics, it was only Quah Zheng Wen and Joseph Schooling.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we afford to let them decide their NS deferment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If the athletes, the swimmers, can decide their own NS deferment, it would take away this additional pressure of what if they have to come back to serve their NS.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Does it mean that their dream of the Olympics is dashed?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third reason – more funding for Singapore Sports School.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Not many parents can spend that $1 million.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we further enhance the Sports School or NSAs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was told that it is not so much the curriculum but because, over there, it gives the swimmers a lot more opportunities to compete.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The fourth reason – sports for every student who is keen in sports.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When I told my friends that I am going to speak in Parliament on this topic, they tell me that, "Yes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need to have more opportunities for every student who is keen in sports to play sports in school." I thought this was already being made available.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Every student got a chance to play because they can play during recess time." How long is recess time?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And they have to buy food and then play sports at the same time?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I studied in a school in a neighbouring country.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I remember that for primary school, we played every day.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Our school only had two table tennis tables, put along the corridor.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have one basketball court which is clay court.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And we played after school until it was dark.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And in my secondary school, it was better equipped.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It had all the sports clubs – badminton club, table tennis club, basketball club, netball club, athletic club.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And that is why I could play many different sports, and I represented the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in five games.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The sporting culture should start from young, not about winning inter-school, and providing platforms to all students to learn the sports of their choice, should be part and parcel of their education.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Sports, we all know, unite people across all ages and cultures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In today's context, this unifying factor is very important.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We worry about race relations and here is a platform that is available for us to tap to unite the citizens.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Sports promote team spirit and imbues camaraderie among the participants.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Look at how people from across races come together before the TV screens to watch the Olympics, the soccer matches, and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is so inspiring to see them united and enjoying themselves as they shout themselves hoarse.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Their athletic feats show the disabled that anything is possible.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have made progress but must not rest on our laurels.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is so much more we can and need to do.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Unlike other countries with a much larger pool of talents and a far longer history of sporting achievements, we have to invest more efforts and wisdom in helping Singapore and her athletes pursue greater heights in the sports arena.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: More importantly, we must not allow stagnation to erase the hard work that everyone, especially our athletes, have put in.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I urge for greater flexibility, empathy and planning to help us keep moving towards our goal of making Singapore a truly sporting nation with a great sporting 	Page: 111 culture at all levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Joseph Schooling's win at the Rio Olympics has inspired the entire nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It showed that a small country like Singapore can dream big and make the dream a reality if we put our hearts and minds to it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We in MCCY are committed to supporting our athletes in achieving their sporting aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our sports excellence programme starts with identifying and developing a pipeline of young athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Singapore Sports School, into its 13th year, offers a unique pathway for young athletes by combining quality education with an excellent sports programme to develop student athletes that can represent Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Sports School offers disciplined and systematic sports training with quality coaching, complemented by support in nutrition, physical and mental development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A special effort is taken to integrate a rigorous academic programme with the training and competition required for athlete development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The contribution of the Sports School is clear.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our Sports School students and alumni shone brightly at the SEA Games last year and we are so proud of them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They contributed a total of 32 gold medals at the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, nearly 40% of Singapore's total haul of 84.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At the same time, we know that there are many high-performing youth athletes in our mainstream schools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To further strengthen the youth sports excellence ecosystem, a new National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) was set up this year to provide specialised support to our youth athletes nationwide.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NYSI works closely with partners in the areas of talent identification and development, youth coaching, sports science and athlete life management.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2013, we introduced our latest iteration of the High-Performance Sports (HPS) system.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our HPS system is still evolving, and we will continue to improve this as we go along.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through Sport Singapore's (SportSG) carding system, athletes are identified based on their actual achievements and assessed potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Support programmes are then customised for the individual needs of the athletes to help them achieve their goals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This targeted, systematic and disciplined process ensures that our resources are optimised in our pursuit of sporting excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Team Singapore athletes have also benefited from the Race to Rio programme since March this year, which provided enhanced support for those seeking to qualify for the Games, and full-time training for 	Page: 112 those who had qualified.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, Joseph Schooling had received various spexGrants, and sports science and medicine support, prior to his being awarded the spexScholarship in 2013.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: He received support, such as training equipment, overseas training camps and competitions, and coaching needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: His University of Texas scholarship imposes conditions on the level of external support he can receive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In bowling, for example, Singapore has produced several world champions, such as Shayna Ng, Joey Yeo and New Hui Fen.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At this year's Olympics, we witnessed breakthrough performances by Quah Zheng Wen and Saiyidah Aisyah in swimming and rowing respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And who can forget Joseph Schooling's and Yip Pin Xiu's record-breaking swims at the Olympics and Paralympics?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: All our Team Singapore athletes have done us tremendously proud.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I agree with Er Dr Lee that the "live" TV broadcast enabled Singaporeans to come together to rally behind our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Loud cheers erupted throughout the island, in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, schools, offices, and other mass gatherings – when Singaporeans dropped whatever they were doing on the morning of 13 August to watch Joseph Schooling's triumphant swim.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Moments like these bind us as one united people and bring us tremendous national pride.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government is certainly supportive of "live" coverage of our Team Singapore athletes and does provide funding support to Mediacorp.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, we are also mindful of the escalating fees for broadcasting such events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is, therefore, a sound and rational approach to leave the negotiation of broadcast rights to Mediacorp and the pay TV operators.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As in many other countries, our broadcasters can harness the marketing potential of the programme through advertising revenue, subscriptions and sponsorships.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It would be unwise to take the position that we should have "live" telecasts regardless of cost, and for the Government to underwrite any amount demanded by rights owners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This would be a poor position to take, particularly while the rights are being negotiated.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Success in high performance sports is borne from the partnership with many stakeholders and not just the Government alone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our NSAs and sports clubs play important roles in developing interest in and providing broad-based support for sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are also instrumental in developing and grooming competitive athletes at all levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Corporate sponsorships have made many local sports events possible, such as the OUE Singapore Open for badminton, Mission Foods Nations Cup for netball.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many of our athletes have benefited from the exposure and the opportunity to compete with the best in the field.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In time to come, we hope Corporate Singapore can play an even bigger role in the HPS system by directly sponsoring our NSAs or athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Businesses can also provide employment opportunities to our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As career after sports weigh on the minds of athletes and their families, we call on more companies to join us in supporting our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Page: 113 We note that NS is a concern for some of our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have been working closely with our NSAs to propose NS deferment for those athletes who require a continuous development pathway and who have consistently demonstrated their sporting potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Besides long-term deferment, there are other opportunities for servicemen to train while fulfilling their full-time NS commitments, such as through the Singapore Armed Forces or Home Team Sportsmen Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our sporting vision goes beyond the success of a select few.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We want Singaporeans to enjoy sports regularly, regardless of sporting ability.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Apart from health benefits, sports also engender social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our sports participation rate is about 55%, up from 44% in 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: ActiveSG, our national sports movement, has about 1.1 million members.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore, a week-long sporting bash to celebrate National Day as One Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our athletes have made their mark on the world stage and inspired Singaporeans back home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Nevertheless, the journey towards fulfilling our sporting vision is a marathon, not a sprint.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While the Government will continue to support our athletes, we must not forget the work it takes to groom a Team Singapore athlete – years of training by the committed athlete, supported by a dedicated team of coaches and sports specialists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And at the heart of it all is the special role of family and friends in providing a secure and encouraging environment for our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We hope that with the support of all stakeholders, we can develop a healthy ecosystem and inspire Singaporeans to Live Better Through Sport.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Er Dr Lee, the debate should last only 30 minutes.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: But you have got a few minutes left.
